title: The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers
abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of the results of F. Najman, "The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers" (Amer. Math. Monthly 117 (2010)). In the Gaussian integers ℤ[i], the equation x⁴ − y⁴ = iz² has only trivial solutions (xyz = 0); the nontrivial solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ = iz² with gcd(x, y, z) = 1 are exactly those with x, y ∈ {±1, ±i} and z = ±i(1 + i), and all its nontrivial solutions are given by x ∈ {±y, ±iy}, z = ±i(1 + i)y²; and the equations x⁴ ± y⁴ = z² have only trivial solutions (a theorem of Hilbert, reproved in the paper). As the paper remarks, the same holds over ℚ(i). The proofs go through the elliptic curves y² = x³ + x and y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), whose groups of ℚ(i)-points, the point at infinity included, are formalized as ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 and ℤ/2 × ℤ/4. Where the paper computes the ranks with a computer program, the formalization determines the ℚ(i)-points directly: the line through a point and its complex conjugate reduces them to rational points, which Fermat's descent determines. 9 theorems and 2 definitions, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
